review.body: Not something this PR introduced, but it's the same family of bug: `ComprehendStartPiiEntitiesDetectionJobCompletedSensor.INTERMEDIATE_STATES` only lists `IN_PROGRESS`, so in non-deferrable mode a job that's still `SUBMITTED` makes `poke()` return True straight away. The waiter retries on `SUBMITTED`, so deferrable mode is fine. Worth a small follow-up PR to add `SUBMITTED` there?
I still don't like the name "Owner", I think that could be confusing now that we have even more auth and multi-team notions in Airflow.
I still don't like the name "Owner", I think that could be confusing now that we have even more auth and multi-team notions in Airflow.

Small nit: the "How authentication works" section in `eks-executor.rst` still says the hook reuses the token and gets a new one a minute before it expires. Could you add a sentence saying that each new token is signed with freshly resolved credentials, and that on a 401 the executor re-reads the connection and retries once with a new token? The new warning will show up in scheduler logs, so it'd help to have it explained there.

comment.body: `_log_aws_identity` below, runs once per hook, but this warning repeats on every `get_conn()`. I think once per hook in the same way makes sense for this warning.

comment.body:
Thank you everyone. Providers are released.

standard and amazon were excluded from this wave. standard will be released as a minor with #76131 reverted, and amazon will be re-cut as 9.40.0rc2 with #76413. Both will go out in an ad-hoc release with its own testing issue, and the amazon PRs already verified here will be carried over as ticked.

I invite everyone to help improve providers for the next release, a list of open issues can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aarea%3Aproviders).

issue.title: No working way to auto-approve a user-scoped list of shell commands and write paths since 0.11.1 (kiro-cli refuses the spec, KAS ignores it)

labels.name: repo-86210cbc
labels.description: Bug: behaviour does not match intent; fix keeps the design

labels.name: repo-86210cbc
labels.description: Waiting for the reporter to answer a question

issue.body:
## Problem

A user-owned kiro-cli v2 agent spec (`~/.kiro/agents/dev.json`) had a tuned `allowedTools` plus `toolsSettings` (`shell.allowedCommands`, `write.allowedPaths`, MCP grants). It ran without needless prompts. Since then, every supported path either refuses the spec or prompts on every shell and write call:

1. **KAS backend (auto-switched on upgrade):** the projection ignores `allowedCommands` and `allowedPaths`, so every shell and write call prompts.
2. **kiro-cli backend on 0.11.0:** worked as before.
3. **kiro-cli backend on 0.11.1+:** the session refuses to start:
   ```
   agent 'dev': /Users/mcmathe1/.kiro/agents/dev.json grants tools the governance ceiling denies, and Kiro Crew does not rewrite a spec it does not own. Remove those entries from its allowedTools or autoApprove, or start the session on KAS, whose projection filters them.
   ```
4. **Removing the flagged entries:** the session starts, but every shell command prompts.
5. **KAS again:** every shell command prompts.
6. **Converting the spec to the kiro-cli v3 format (JSON and markdown):** no auto-approved shell commands either way.

The remaining workaround is session-wide Trust mode, which is broader than the user wants.

## Expected

- A user can declare a persistent, scoped allowlist (shell command patterns and write paths), per agent, that is answered without a prompt.
- Crew's deny floor, sensitive-path check and governance still run before that allowlist is applied (the shape proposed in #11200 and #25365).
- If the ceiling rejects some entries, the session starts anyway with those entries ignored, and the user is told which entries were dropped. A hard startup refusal leaves no usable middle ground.
- The docs state which spec format and backend supports command-level and path-level auto-approval.

**Environment:** kirocrew 0.11.2 (regression first seen in 0.11.1), macOS, dashboard sessions.

**Related:** #11200, #25365, #29436, #25317, #20450

Submitted by Kiro

comment.body:
Another case that hits this on KAS, split out with its cause in #31859: a scoped `ask` rule makes every call of that built-in prompt, not just the calls it matches.

Our team's agent specs allow the shell and only ask for sudo:

```json
{"capability": "shell", "effect": "allow"},
{"capability": "shell", "match": ["sudo *"], "effect": "ask"}
```

On kirocrew 0.12.0.9, `withhold_answered_under_authored_rules` reads any non-allow rule as a restriction on the whole capability and ignores its `match`. Crew then stops answering the spec's `shell` grant, so every shell command prompts, not only `sudo`. Removing the `sudo *` rule brings the grant back. The same spec runs shell commands without routine prompts on the kiro-cli backend.

comment.body:
> Would you be open to a follow-up that makes the hook use the AWS connection's credentials by default when it has any, like the other AWS hooks do, and falls back to the credential chain otherwise?

Thanks for the review @seanghaeli 

That's for sure out of scope for this docs PR, but I think there is something to be done there. Though we need to be careful to not use `config` when the user doesn't actually want to since it doesn't perform as well as credential_chain. Off the top of my head: we default the to "aws_default", I'm not sure we want to bail to `config` in that case, since we can't be sure the user is really asking us to. But, I'd say that we can assume that if they provide a non-default connection id.

+
+DuckDB on AWS Connection
+========================
+
+The DuckDB on AWS connection type is used by
+:class:`~airflow.providers.amazon.aws.hooks.duckdb.AwsDuckDBHook` to query data in Amazon S3 with
+DuckDB. See :doc:`../operators/duckdb` for usage.
+
+Two connections are involved:
+
+* A **DuckDB on AWS** (``duckdb_aws``) connection which configures DuckDB itself, i.e.: *which DuckDB database and with what settings*.
+  Its id is what you pass to
+  :class:`~airflow.providers.duckdb.operators.duckdb.DuckDBExecuteQueryOperator` as ``conn_id``, and its
+  type is also what selects :class:`~airflow.providers.amazon.aws.hooks.duckdb.AwsDuckDBHook`.
+* An **AWS** (``aws``) connection says *which AWS identity*, i.e.: keys or role, region, endpoint, etc. The DuckDB
+  connection points at it through ``aws_conn_id``, which defaults to ``aws_default``.
+
+Credentials stay in the usual :ref:`AWS connection <howto/connection:aws>`. The ``duckdb_aws`` connection can be empty
+(though it must exist) and often will be with DuckDB's ability to use in-memory databases. Create it, name it whatever
+you like, and leave every field blank to get an in-memory database.
+
+Configuring the Connection
+--------------------------
+
+Database path (optional)
+    Path to a DuckDB database file, for example ``/tmp/analytics.duckdb``. Leave empty for an
+    in-memory database.
+
+Extra (optional)
+    A JSON object. Every parameter of ``AwsDuckDBHook`` can be set here, and ``hook_params`` on the
+    operator overrides it per task. The AWS keys are:
+
+    * ``aws_conn_id``: the AWS connection to take credentials from. Defaults to ``aws_default``. Set
+      it to ``null`` to use no Airflow connection and let the AWS SDK find credentials in the
+      environment.
+    * ``region_name``: region for the S3 secret. Defaults to the region of the AWS connection.
+    * ``credential_strategy``: ``credential_chain`` (default), ``config`` or ``none``. See
+      :ref:`howto/operator:duckdb_aws:credentials`.
+    * ``credential_chain``: the providers DuckDB's credential chain consults, for example
+      ``"env;config;sts;instance"``.
+    * ``s3_endpoint_url``: S3 endpoint override, for an S3-compatible service or a VPC endpoint.
+      Defaults to ``endpoint_url`` from the AWS connection extra.
+    * ``secret_name``: name of the DuckDB secret to create. Defaults to ``airflow_aws``.
+
+    The DuckDB engine keys, such as ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` and ``extensions``, are the same as
+    in the :doc:`DuckDB connection <apache-airflow-providers-duckdb:connections/duckdb>`. One default
+    differs: ``autoinstall_extensions`` is ``true`` here, so the ``httpfs`` and ``aws`` extensions
+    are installed if they are missing.
+
+Examples
+--------
+
+An in-memory database with explicit resource limits, using ``aws_default``:
+
+.. code-block:: json
+
+    {
+      "memory_limit": "2GB",
+      "threads": 4
+    }
+
+A database file, with credentials from a specific AWS connection:
+
+.. code-block:: bash
+
+    export AIRFLOW_CONN_DUCKDB_AWS_DEFAULT='{
+        "conn_type": "duckdb_aws",
+        "host": "/tmp/analytics.duckdb",
+        "extra": {"aws_conn_id": "aws_analytics", "region_name": "eu-west-1"}

issue.title: KAS: a scoped "ask" rule or toolsSettings.write.allowedPaths makes every call of that built-in prompt

labels.name: repo-86210cbc
labels.description: Bug: behaviour does not match intent; fix keeps the design

issue.body:
## Problem

On KAS, Crew answers permission requests for built-ins that a spec grants in `allowedTools` (#25317). `withhold_answered_under_authored_rules` then drops a built-in from that set when the spec restricts its capability in any way, and it ignores the restriction's scope. Two common spec shapes hit this:

1. **A scoped `ask` rule.** `{"capability": "shell", "match": ["sudo *"], "effect": "ask"}` next to a plain shell allow. `_restricted_by_rules` reads it as a restriction on all of `shell`, so every command prompts, not only `sudo`.
2. **`toolsSettings.write.allowedPaths`.** `authored_restricted_capabilities` treats any `toolsSettings` entry for a built-in as a restriction. `allowedPaths` is a grant, but it withholds `fs_write`, so every write prompts, even inside the allowed paths. The shell's `allowedCommands` is already exempted (`without_allowed_commands`); nothing does the same for `allowedPaths`.

The same spec runs shell commands and writes without routine prompts on the kiro-cli backend. Since a saved Kiro CLI pick now resolves to KAS, those users get the prompts by default.

## Evidence

kirocrew 0.12.0.9, kiro-cli 3.1.0, Linux. Spec (trimmed):

```json
"allowedTools": ["read", "write", "shell", "grep", "glob"],
"toolsSettings": {"write": {"allowedPaths": ["./**"]}},
"permissions": {"rules": [
  {"capability": "fs_read", "effect": "allow"},
  {"capability": "fs_write", "match": ["./**"], "effect": "allow"},
  {"capability": "shell", "effect": "allow"},
  {"capability": "shell", "match": ["sudo *"], "effect": "ask"}
]}
```

Output of `crew_answered_builtins`, then `withhold_answered_under_authored_rules` (`acp/kas_permissions.py`), on this spec:

| Spec | Crew answers |
|---|---|
| as is | fs_read, glob, grep |
| without the `sudo *` ask | + execute_bash |
| without `toolsSettings.write` | + fs_write |
| without both | execute_bash, fs_read, fs_write, glob, grep |

## Expected

- A scoped `ask` or `deny` rule withholds only the calls its `match` covers. Here Crew still answers `ls`, and `sudo ls` prompts.
- `write.allowedPaths` is read as a grant, like `allowedCommands`: Crew answers writes inside those paths, after its deny floor and sensitive-path checks.

## Related

#30017 (its last comment hits case 2), #30165, #25317, #25539

---
Drafted-by: Kiro (Claude Opus 5.5); reviewed by @o-nikolas before posting

issue.body:
I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:

issue.body:
I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:


## Provider [alibaba: 4.0.0rc1](https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow-providers-alibaba/4.0.0rc1)
   - [x] [Remove deprecated get_hook property from OSSKeySensor (#76127)](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/76127): @shahar1

issue.body:

(72 Hours is the minimum reaction time you can expect from volunteers) - we sometimes miss notifications.

In case of an existing issue, reference it using one of the following:

* closes: #ISSUE
* related: #ISSUE
-->

`logical_date`, `start_date` and `end_date` are stored as datetime in the database.

When building the current message for the Kafka Event Producer plugin, the dates are converted to string using `str()`. As a result, the date is formatted with a space instead of a `T`, which is a non-standard time format and it requires a custom method to validate as a json schema.

This patch changes the format of the date, from `str()` to `isoformat()` so that it's more standardized and the date is in a valid format for a json schema and doesn't require a special function to validate the date-time.

This is what the date looks like in the two shapes

* `str(dt)`
    * `2026-10-30 14:40:05.123456+00:00`
* `dt.isoformat()`
    * `2026-10-30T14:40:05.123456+00:00`

Empty dates now default to null instead of `""`.

issue.title: Use only the configured auth type when creating tokens in the FAB auth manager
issue.body:
`FabAuthManager.create_token()` checked a username and password against the database for every `AUTH_TYPE`: after LDAP, and also for authentication types that never use a local password (OAuth, remote user), where users are stored without one. It now checks only against the configured authentication type (`AUTH_DB` or `AUTH_LDAP`) and issues no token for the others, which matches Flask-AppBuilder's own login views. A password made only of NUL bytes is also rejected as empty, as Flask-AppBuilder's login API does.

A provider changelog note describes the behaviour change for LDAP deployments that relied on the database fallback for API tokens.

issue.body:
`S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` documented that S3 SSL certificates are verified by default, but `s3_verify` defaulted to `False`, which disabled verification for every S3 call the operator made. This changes the default to `None`, so the S3 hook follows the connection's / botocore's default (verification on), the same as the other AWS transfer operators. Users who relied on the old behaviour can pass `s3_verify=False` explicitly; a changelog note says so.

Related: airflow-s/airflow-s#717

issue.title: Fix Google Cloud Logging task log reads before Airflow 3.4

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: Google (including GCP) related issues

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: Set by triage when all criteria pass, or by the fork CI reconciler when fork CI is green.

issue.body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
     https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 -->

related: https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/74204, #68240, #68293

<!-- HUMAN SUMMARY - AGENTS DO NOT MODIFY -->
On Airflow 3, the Google Cloud Logging remote log reader now filters by `run_id` (matched case-sensitively) and `map_index` to match the labels written from the task process context, and supports runs without a logical date. Airflow 2 keeps using `execution_date` and is unaffected. For map index 0, the filter also matches older entries without a `map_index` label.
Entries are also labelled with their log file path, so lines without task context, like `print()` output on workers before 3.4 and triggerer output before 3.2.2, are found too.
This PR fixes 5 reader bugs:

- Task logs not appearing on Airflow 3.3.x, or on 3.2.2 and later with a custom `REMOTE_TASK_LOG`
- An `AttributeError` for runs without a logical date
- Mapped tasks sharing one filter before Airflow 3.4
- `print()` output never appearing on workers before Airflow 3.4
- Deferred tasks' triggerer output never appearing before Airflow 3.2.2 (with a custom REMOTE_TASK_LOG)

<!-- END OF HUMAN SUMMARY -->

<details><summary>AI Summary</summary>

Since Airflow 3.2.2, `CloudLoggingRemoteLogIO` labels each entry with the values the task process binds into its log context: `ti_id`, `dag_id`, `task_id`, `run_id`, `try_number` and `map_index`. The reader still built its filter from a `logical_date` label, which no Airflow 3 writer sets. As a result:

- **Airflow 3.2.2 to 3.3.x:** the reader matches nothing. Task logs written to Cloud Logging never show in the UI.
- **Any Airflow 3 version:** reading logs for a Dag run without a logical date fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'isoformat'`.
- **Mapped tasks before 3.4:** the filter has no `map_index`, so all map indexes would share one filter.

From 3.4 on, #74204 matches entries by `ti_id`. The label fallback in this PR covers older Airflow versions, and runs without a logical date on every version.

The reader now filters on `run_id` and `map_index` on Airflow 3. `run_id` is matched with an anchored regex, because Cloud Logging compares strings with `=` ignoring letter case. Airflow 2 still uses `execution_date`, which is what its handler writes. The writer used to skip `map_index` 0 because the check was truthy, so the first mapped task's existing entries have no `map_index` label. The filter for map index 0 also accepts entries that have no `map_index` label.

On Airflow 3 nothing calls `set_context`, so `CloudLoggingTaskHandler` never wrote `logical_date` labels for task logs there. Dropping `logical_date` from the Airflow 3 filter makes no existing entry unreadable.

On workers before Airflow 3.4, lines a task prints to stdout and lines the supervisor logs on its own reach Cloud Logging without the task's log context, so they carry no task labels and no label filter can find them. The writer now also labels every entry with `log_path`, the task log file it belongs to. The reader matches that label against the path `FileTaskHandler` passes to `read()`, but only for entries without task labels (and, from 3.4, without `ti_id`), so lines another try wrote under the same path stay out.

Verified on the official Airflow 3.3.2 image writing to Cloud Logging, with local log copies deleted, for a plain task and a task mapped over two values, in runs with and without a logical date:

- **Provider built from main:** the reader returns no lines, and runs without a logical date fail with the `AttributeError`.
- **This PR:** each task instance shows exactly its own logger and `print()` lines. Entries written earlier by the provider built from main are also found, except their `print()` lines, which have no labels to match.

Known limitations, none of them regressions:

- **Entries already written without labels:** `print()` and supervisor lines written by earlier provider releases, and every entry written on Airflow 3.0.0 to 3.2.1 by them, stay unreadable. Entries written from this release on are found by `log_path`.
- **Custom log filename templates without `try_number`:** context-less lines of every try share one path and are all shown, as they would be in the local log file.
- **`CloudLoggingTaskHandler` as the task handler:** the `log_path` match covers the remote log reader (`CloudLoggingRemoteLogIO`) only. On Airflow 3, a setup that keeps `StackdriverTaskHandler` as the task handler with a custom `REMOTE_TASK_LOG` still reads, and links to, only the lines with task labels.
- **Downloading all tries on 3.4:** this path drops the `ti_id` condition. It relies on `map_index`, which can differ from the stored index for region tasks.

This picks up the part of #68293 that #74204 did not cover, and builds on that PR's investigation.
</details>

I'd do Vincent's suggestion in this PR rather than a follow-up. The subject type is only lost at the token exchange: `issue_execution_token` mints the same `{"sub": ..., "scope": "execution"}` token for task instances and callbacks, and both callers know which one they are. Could you add a claim there, e.g. `sub_type: Literal["task_instance", "callback"] = "task_instance"` on `TIClaims`, set it to `"callback"` from `routes/callbacks.py`, and have `get_team_name_dep` and `has_xcom_access` pick the task or callback lookup from it?

The claims model allows extra fields and `JWTReissueMiddleware` copies them on refresh, so older API servers still accept the token, and the default keeps legacy and in-process tokens working. It also lets you drop the `UNION ALL` lookup, the ambiguous-subject 403 and its test, so the PR should end up smaller.

issue.title: Fix env var names in AWS ECS and Lambda executor setup docs

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: AWS/Amazon - related issues

issue.body:
The AWS-console setup steps in the ECS and Lambda executor docs told users to set
`AIRFLOW__ECS_EXECUTOR__SECURITY_GROUPS`, `AIRFLOW__ECS_EXECUTOR__SUBNETS` and
`AIRFLOW__LAMBDA_EXECUTOR__QUEUE_URL`. The executors read the `aws_ecs_executor` and
`aws_lambda_executor` config sections (`CONFIG_GROUP_NAME` in
`aws/executors/ecs/utils.py` and `aws/executors/aws_lambda/utils.py`), so Airflow
silently ignored those variables. ECS tasks then started without the security
groups and subnets needed to reach the RDS metadata database, and the Lambda
executor had no SQS queue URL.

The CLI-based sections of the same pages already use the correct
`AIRFLOW__AWS_ECS_EXECUTOR__*` / `AIRFLOW__AWS_LAMBDA_EXECUTOR__*` names; these were
the only three references with the wrong prefix in the repository.

+The triggerer runs three kinds of trigger: the trigger of a :doc:`deferred task </authoring-and-scheduling/deferring>`,
+a triggerer callback (for example a deadline alert's ``AsyncCallback``), and an
+:doc:`asset watcher </authoring-and-scheduling/event-scheduling>`. ``GET /api/v2/triggers`` lists all of them the same
+way: what each one runs for, which triggerer runs it, and how it is doing. Trigger arguments are never returned.
+
+Status
+------
+
+``pending``
+    Not picked up by a triggerer yet.
+
+``running``
+    On a live triggerer and not failed since it last recovered. For an asset watcher this does not mean the
+    source it watches is healthy, only that the trigger is not raising; ``last_event_at`` says when it last fired.
+
+``failing``
+    On a live triggerer, and it raised or ended without yielding an event since it last recovered.
+    ``consecutive_failures``, ``first_failed_at`` and ``last_error`` say how often, since when and why. A trigger
+    that is still wanted, such as an asset watcher, is re-created within seconds and stays ``failing`` until it
+    recovers: it yields an event, or stays up for two minutes.
+
+``orphaned``
+    Its triggerer stopped sending heartbeats. Another triggerer takes it over within
+    ``[triggerer] triggerer_health_check_threshold`` seconds.
+
+``triggerer_hostname`` is the host of the triggerer the trigger is assigned to; each live triggerer's heartbeat is
+on the health endpoint. The failure count is kept on the trigger, so it carries over when the triggerer restarts
+or another triggerer takes the trigger over. ``last_error`` is kept after a recovery.
+
+A trigger is listed only while its owner still refers to it. Once a deferred task resumes or fails, a callback
+finishes, or a watcher is removed, the trigger is deleted on the triggerer's next cleanup, and its outcome stays
+with its owner: the task instance's state and logs, the callback's state and logs.
+
+During a rolling upgrade from a version that does not record trigger owners, a deferred task's or callback's
+trigger created by the older components is listed only once a triggerer of this version picks it up and records its
+owner, and a trigger still run by an older triggerer is never ``failing``, since older triggerers do not record
+failures.

+-----
+
+Each trigger names what it runs for: ``task_instance`` (Dag, run, task, map index, try and state), ``callback``

+of the Dag run whose deadline the callback belongs to. In the other direction, a task instance's ``trigger`` and an
+asset's ``watchers`` (with ``status`` and ``trigger_id``) link to the trigger.

issue.title: Fix masked failure reason for deferrable EMR Serverless jobs

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: AWS/Amazon - related issues

issue.body:
On a deferrable EMR Serverless job **failure or timeout**, the real failure reason was masked by a `KeyError`, and the raised message could not tell the two outcomes apart.

## The bug

`EmrServerlessStartJobTrigger` emits a success event carrying `job_details` (`{application_id, job_id}`), but a **failure** event carrying only `{status, message}`. `EmrServerlessStartJobOperator.execute_complete` then read `event["job_details"]["application_id"]` to cancel the run before raising — so on any real failure it raised `KeyError: 'job_details'`, hiding the actual reason. On resume `execute()` has not run, so `self.job_id` is also unset, meaning the cancel had no run id to act on even if `job_details` had been present.

Even with the `KeyError` out of the way, the trigger reported a terminal job failure and an exhausted poll identically (`status: "failure"`), so the operator could only raise the ambiguous "failed or timed out" and always attempted a cancel — a call that errors on a run that has already reached a terminal state.

Found while validating #73701 on live AWS: a genuine job failure surfaced only as `KeyError: 'job_details'` in the task logs, not the underlying Spark error.

## The fix

**Trigger** (`EmrServerlessStartJobTrigger.run`)

- The failure event now carries `job_details`, consistent with the success event.
- It also carries a `failure_type` derived from the dedicated waiter exceptions, so the operator does not have to string-match the message: `WaiterTerminalFailure` → `terminal`, `WaiterMaxAttemptsError` → `timeout`, anything else → `error`.

**Operator** (`EmrServerlessStartJobOperator.execute_complete`)

- Reads the run id from the event (falling back to `self`) so it works on resume.
- Raises an outcome-specific `RuntimeError` that includes the real reason: `EMR Serverless job <id> timed out in deferrable mode: <reason>` vs `EMR Serverless job <id> failed in deferrable mode: <reason>`. `RuntimeError` replaces `AirflowException`, which provider code avoids.
- Cancels the run **only on a timeout**, when it may still be active and would otherwise be orphaned. A terminal failure is already done, so it is no longer cancelled (dropping a cancel that always errored). An unexpected trigger error does not cancel either, to avoid killing a possibly healthy run.
- The cancel is guarded with `except (BotoCoreError, ClientError)` and logged, so a cancel-time boto error (the run reached a terminal state in the meantime, a connection error, …) cannot mask the real reason.

This is an independent, pre-existing bug on `main`, unrelated to #73701 / #73702 — it was just noticed while validating them.

## Testing

New tests, each failing without this change:

- Trigger: a failure event carries `job_details` and the right `failure_type` for a terminal failure, a poll timeout and an unexpected error (parametrized).
- Operator: a timeout cancels the run with the exact `applicationId` / `jobRunId` and raises the timed-out message with the waiter reason.
- Operator: a terminal failure raises the real reason and does not cancel.
- Operator: a failure event without `job_details` raises the reason instead of `KeyError`.

issue.title: Fix deferrable EmrCreateJobFlowOperator ignoring wait_policy

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: AWS/Amazon - related issues

issue.body:
In deferrable mode, `EmrCreateJobFlowOperator` ignores `wait_policy=WaitPolicy.WAIT_FOR_STEPS_COMPLETION`: the task is marked successful as soon as the EMR cluster is running, while its steps are still executing, and a failure after that point goes unnoticed. The non-deferrable path correctly waits for the cluster to terminate.

#61195 made the operator pass the waiter selected from `wait_policy` (`job_flow_terminated` for `WAIT_FOR_STEPS_COMPLETION`) to `EmrCreateJobFlowTrigger`, but the trigger never added `waiter_name` to its `serialized_fields`. The triggerer rebuilds the trigger from `serialize()`, so it always fell back to the default `job_flow_waiting` waiter, which already succeeds on `RUNNING`.

This adds `waiter_name` to the trigger's serialized kwargs. Triggers deferred before this change have no `waiter_name` in their stored kwargs and keep rebuilding with the default, so their behaviour does not change.

Tests:

- `TestEmrCreateJobFlowTrigger.test_serialization` pinned the serialized kwargs without `waiter_name`; it now covers the default and `job_flow_terminated` waiters and checks that a trigger rebuilt from the serialized kwargs keeps the waiter.
- New `test_create_job_flow_deferrable_serializes_wait_policy_waiter` checks, for each `WaitPolicy`, that the deferred trigger's serialized kwargs carry the matching waiter.

Both fail without the fix (kwargs mismatch / `KeyError: 'waiter_name'`) and pass with it. Also ran locally: `triggers/test_emr.py`, `triggers/test_serialization.py`, `operators/test_emr_create_job_flow.py` and `test_deferred_hook_configuration.py` (295 passed, 35 skipped by that test's allowlist), `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`, `scripts/ci/prek/check_trigger_serialize_init.py`, and `mypy` on the changed module. The tests ran on Windows with local stubs for `os.register_at_fork` and `fcntl`, which Airflow needs at import time; CI covers Linux.

issue.body:
We are kindly requesting that contributors to [Apache Airflow RC 3.4.0rc3](https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow/3.4.0rc3/) help test the RC.

Please let us know by checking the box / commenting if the change is addressed in the latest RC.

## Significant Changes

> Full details (migration notes, changed endpoints, behavioural changes) for each item are in the [3.4.0 release notes](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/v3-4-test/RELEASE_NOTES.rst). The entries below are for test-tracking only.

- [ ] Dag Importer for non-Python Dags (#72369, #73728, #73853, #74020, #74084, #74333, #74586): @dilnazanlid @uranusjr
- [ ] Unify executor workload queues under ``BaseExecutor.executor_queues`` (#63491): @anishgirianish
- [ ] psycopg3 is now the default Postgres driver (#68496): @Dev-iL
- [ ] Asset-triggered Dags create one run per event by default (#68517): @renat-sagut
- [ ] Custom graph colors return via ``ui_color`` and ``ui_fgcolor`` (#68760): @pierrejeambrun
- [ ] ``validate_key`` now raises ``ValueError`` instead of ``AirflowException`` (#68890): @23tae

comment.body: Tested multi-team today. I found a few issues but they're either minor or not new for 3.4. I will start putting out some PRs, but since multi-team is still an experimental feature and again most of them are quite small, I don't think they should block the 3.4 release

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -570,17 +627,27 @@ def end(self, heartbeat_interval=10):
         try:
             while True:
                 self.sync()
-                if not self.active_workers:
+                if not self.active_workers and not self._run_task_futures:
                     break
                 time.sleep(heartbeat_interval)
         except Exception:
             # We catch any and all exceptions because otherwise they would bubble
             # up and kill the scheduler process.
             self.log.exception("Failed to end %s", self.__class__.__name__)
+        if self._run_task_pool is not None:
+            self._run_task_pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
 
     def terminate(self):
         """Kill all ECS processes by calling Boto3's StopTask API."""
         try:
+            if self._run_task_pool is not None:
+                # A RunTask call still in flight may start an ECS task after the StopTask calls below:
+                # wait for the calls already started, and drop the ones not started yet.
+                self._run_task_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True)
+                for future, ecs_task in list(self._run_task_futures.items()):
+                    del self._run_task_futures[future]
+                    if not future.cancelled():
+                        self._handle_run_task_response(ecs_task, future.result)
comment.body: if `_handle_run_task_response` raises here (credentials error, or the "should never happen" EcsExecutorException), the StopTask loop at line 651 is skipped for every running task. Could each result be handled in its own try, so the StopTask calls still run?

issue.title: KubernetesExecutor: let each team connect to its own cluster
issue.body:
### Description

KubernetesExecutor reads the settings it uses to connect to a cluster (`in_cluster`, `config_file`, `cluster_context`, `verify_ssl`, `ssl_ca_cert`) from the global `[kubernetes_executor]` section, even in multi-team mode. Namespace, pod template and the other pod settings are team-scoped, but every team connects to the same cluster. The `client_factory` and `async_client_factory` settings (#73014) can be set per team, but the factory is called with no arguments, so it can't tell which team it's building a client for.

This also affects KubernetesExecutor subclasses that bring their own client factory, such as `AwsEksExecutor` (#74399). The only way for a subclass to install its factory is through the `[kubernetes_executor] client_factory` setting, so a plain KubernetesExecutor in the same scope (both global, or the same team) picks it up too and connects to the subclass's cluster.

Proposed change: build the executor's clients with the team name, so the connection settings resolve per team and a factory is told which team it's for. Let a subclass declare its client factory on the class rather than through config, and have the scheduler and the pod watcher use it.

### Use case/motivation

Multi-team deployments where teams run tasks on different Kubernetes clusters, and deployments that run KubernetesExecutor next to a subclass with its own client factory, for example while moving from one to the other.

### Related issues

#73014, #74399 (review discussion: https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/74399#discussion_r4288802873, https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/74399#discussion_r4288848035)

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes

comment.body:
This counts every scope that has any executor, then compares its [kubernetes_executor] namespace. A scope with no Kubernetes executor never uses that setting, but it still has the built-in value default. So with CeleryExecutor;team_a=KubernetesExecutor and no namespace set, --team team_a refuses ("also used by the global executors"), though Celery makes no pods there. The "another cluster" hint is also wrong for that case.

Could we only count scopes that run a KubernetesExecutor? Something like:

```python
scopes = {
    n.team_name
    for n in ExecutorLoader.get_executor_names(validate_teams=False)
    if n.team_name != team_name
    and issubclass(ExecutorLoader.import_executor_cls(n)[0], KubernetesExecutor)
}
```
The shared-with-global and shared-with-team tests would then need a Kubernetes executor in the other scope, since the global setup and team_b only run LocalExecutor there.

issue.title: Allow ECS exit codes to fail tasks without retrying

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: AWS/Amazon - related issues

issue.body:
Allow Dag authors to stop retries for known application failures reported by an ECS container. For example, with `retries=2` and `fail_on_exit_code=2`, an invalid-input exit code fails the Airflow task after its first attempt, while other exit codes retain the normal retry behavior.

The option accepts an integer or a container of integers, matching the existing `skip_on_exit_code` interface. It defaults to `None` and applies to synchronous and resumed deferrable execution. Exit code zero remains successful, and a missing exit code is not inferred as a match.

This completes the fail-without-retry part originally proposed in #47256; #63274 subsequently added the skip option. The decision uses the existing DescribeTasks response, avoiding exception-message parsing or an additional AWS lookup to recover the exit code. A selected code raises `AirflowFailException`, including on versions supporting generic `retry_policy`.

For multiple containers, a matching nonzero code from any stopped container takes precedence over sibling container failures and skip codes, irrespective of container order. Fail also takes precedence when the same code appears in both options. Existing task-level startup, host-termination and AWS API error handling remains in place. These semantics and the no-wait limitation are documented.

Validation on upstream `5799660c4d41e95b8c3ce836bd9003c3e4f3a998`, Linux/amd64 Breeze, Python 3.10.21:

- 43 SDK-boundary regression cases in the existing `test_ecs.py`; 152 related ECS operator/hook/trigger tests passed with two workers on current main.
- On Airflow 3.0.6, the broader ECS selection passed: 282 passed, 10 skipped.
- On Airflow 2.11.1, the same operator/hook/trigger selection passed: 152 passed. This used source providers in an isolated Breeze container, excluding incompatible Airflow 3-only providers while preserving the older FAB dependency required by Airflow 2.
- 11 existing Task SDK no-retry/retry-policy tests passed. Regular/manual prek, provider mypy, commit-message checks and `git diff --check` passed. Selective-check was run against the complete PR diff.

AWS responses use SDK Stubbers. Live AWS, separately deployed worker/triggerer processes, and the full dependent-provider/version CI matrix were not run locally.

issue.title: Document S3-compatible remote logging in the Amazon provider

labels.name: repo-2cce738a
labels.description: AWS/Amazon - related issues

issue.body:
Add a docs recipe and a system-test example Dag showing how to reuse the existing Amazon provider S3 integration against any S3-compatible object store.

The Amazon provider already talks to S3-compatible endpoints: pointing an `aws` connection at a custom `endpoint_url` makes the S3 task handler and `ObjectStoragePath("s3://...")` write to that endpoint instead of AWS S3. That capability is not documented from the "bring your own S3-compatible bucket" angle, so users rediscover the connection extras (`endpoint_url`, `region_name`, path-style addressing) by trial and error. This change writes that path down. Amazon S3 is the baseline, and the recipe notes that the same steps work against other S3-compatible services (for example Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, and MinIO), using placeholder endpoints so the steps are copy-pasteable against any of them.

The change is intentionally small and additive: it adds documentation and one example, and touches no provider or core code.

What is included:

- `providers/amazon/docs/logging/s3-compatible-remote-logging.rst`: a recipe that maps S3-compatible credentials onto the AWS connection fields, configures `[logging]` remote logging through that connection, verifies the logs land in the bucket, reuses the same connection for `ObjectStoragePath` Dag data, and sketches a generic bucket-event ingestion pattern. It cross-references the existing `write-logs-amazon-s3` handler doc rather than restating it, and it is picked up automatically by the globbed toctree in `providers/amazon/docs/logging/index.rst` (no manual index edit needed).
- `providers/amazon/tests/system/amazon/aws/example_s3_compatible_object_storage.py`: an input to transform to output example Dag built on `ObjectStoragePath`, sitting alongside the other `example_s3*.py` system tests and wired through the standard `get_test_run(dag)` harness. Bucket and connection id are read from the environment so the example carries no secrets; the default placeholder skips the system test until a real bucket is configured, and each run writes under a `AIRFLOW_CTX_DAG_RUN_ID` subdirectory to avoid overwriting parallel or repeated runs.

Scope notes for reviewers:

- No new operator, hook, bundle, or `provider.yaml` entry: this documents existing behavior, so there is nothing new for the registry to pick up.
- The framing is generic S3-compatible object storage. AWS S3 is the baseline; other providers are named only as interchangeable examples with placeholder endpoints.
- No newsfragment: per the contributor docs, `providers/` changelogs are regenerated from `git log` by the release managers and do not consume per-PR newsfragments.

Testing:

- Built the provider docs locally and confirmed the new page renders and appears under the Amazon provider "Logging for Tasks" section, with the cross-reference to the S3 task handler resolving.
- The example Dag is a system test (network access to a real bucket required to execute against a live endpoint) and follows the existing `example_s3*.py` structure; the module imports and parses cleanly and exposes `test_run` via `get_test_run(dag)`.
- Ran targeted Ruff format/check on the new Python file after Python review fixes; docs-only follow-ups were checked with `git diff --check`.
